title: Admin elevation runbook and override controls for critical incidents
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a formalized, auditable admin elevation runbook and override controls to be used during P0/P1 incidents or when normal RBAC v2 paths cannot satisfy an urgent recovery operation. This ticket covers: SSO/SAML short-lived elevated sessions, two-person overrides, audit logging policy and schema, automated de-escalation, emergency justification capture, and operator ergonomics in Console/CLI. This is intended to replace ad-hoc break-glass practices and integrate with RBAC v2, KMS/HSM-backed key escrow, and SIEM ingestion for forensic readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook exists in Confluence and is referenced from incident playbooks
Temporary elevated sessions can be created via SSO SAML assertion with explicit justification and TTL (default 1 hour), audited to the central audit pipeline
Two-person approval enforced for 'high-scope' escalations (affects production network/config), with the approver distinct from the requester
Automatic de-escalation occurs at TTL expiry and any manual extension requires re-approval and is logged
All administrative actions taken during elevated sessions are tagged and exported to SIEM with raw KV-cache and model-run identifiers where relevant
RBAC v2 mapping documents updated to include emergency override entitlements and restrictive default policies
Security team sign-off recorded and security_review_required flag cleared after review
Console UI displays active emergency sessions and last justification for easy audit checks
implementation_notes: Add an 'elevation' grant type to RBAC v2 model: minimal scope by default, opt-in extension via approver flow
Implement SAML assertion extension with 'elevation:reason' and 'elevation:ttl' attributes; enforcement in the token service
Leverage KMS/HSM to sign temporary admin tokens; store signing audit record in encrypted audit store
Design a two-person approval microservice (stateless) with signed approvals persisted to audit log; approvals are time-bound (max 4 hours)
Console: add an 'Elevations' panel for on-call and security to see live elevated sessions; API endpoint: /admin/elevations
CLI: 'redwood elevate --reason "" --scope ""' uses SSO flow and returns a short-lived token; requires interactive reauth if run locally
Audit pipeline: add elevation metadata fields (requester, approver, scope, justification, start_ts, end_ts, token_id) to the existing audit schema
SIEM: forward elevation events with high-fidelity logs (raw request/response IDs obfuscated) and retain for 2 years per compliance needs
testing_plan: Unit tests for token service enforcement of 'elevation:ttl' and scope reduction
Integration test: SAML flow with elevation attrs simulated via test IdP to ensure token issuance and expiry
E2E incident drill in staging that triggers a high-scope elevation and verifies two-person approval path, audit generation, and automatic de-escalation
Access reviews: run a periodic script to list active elevations and verify their TTLs and audit entries
Load test the approvals microservice with concurrent emergency requests to ensure latency < 250ms for approval checks under 99th percentile
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): Deploy to staging, run 3 incident drills with on-call, iterate on operator feedback
Phase 2 (canary): Deploy to 10% of Dedicated clusters and internal Console users; monitor false-positive/negative rates for approval enforcement
Phase 3 (general): Flip feature flag for all customers but hide UI controls unless customer has 'emergency-overrides' entitlement
Communication: publish runbook, update on-call SOPs, and host a 1-hour training session for on-call and security engineers
Post-rollout audit: collect the first 30 elevation events and run a security review for correctness and policy gaps
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert when there are >3 concurrent 'high-scope' elevations across regions (PagerDuty paging to security-oncall)
Dashboard: live list of active elevations with requester, approver, start_ts, ttl, and scope summary
Audit ingestion has a daily job verifying retention and completeness; alert on missing fields or failed exports to SIEM
Periodic (weekly) lint job to detect elevated sessions that lack justification or approver signature
comments: 2025-02-10 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket. Core goal is to eliminate ad-hoc SSH/privileged escalation and provide an auditable, SSO-aligned path for necessary emergency tasks.

2025-02-11 - Priya Desai (Security): +1 on two-person approval for high-scope work. We need to define 'high-scope' precisely; propose: any change that touches customer crypto, KMS, network ACLs, or production model binaries.
2025-02-11 - Ravi Kapoor: Added initial implementation notes. Will prototype SAML attr approach with our Okta test tenant this week.

2025-02-12 - Jonah Li (Platform): Concern: two-person approval may add latency during P0. Suggest a fast-path for specific on-call roles with stricter logging (5-min grace) — security to weigh tradeoffs.

2025-02-12 - Priya Desai (Security): Tradeoff accepted only if fast-path is limited to infra-ops SRE role and logged with continuous screen recording to audit store. Security prefers no fast-path but ok with conservative allowance for critical recovery.

2025-02-13 - Design review by Marissa Chen: Console Elevations panel mockups shared at https://drive.redwood/company/designs/elevations-v1. Feedback: make justification field mandatory and visible in listing; color-code by scope severity.
2025-02-14 - QA (Ben Ortiz): I added test cases for TTL enforcement and extension approval. Found a bug where token extension didn't refresh audit.end_ts; filed ENG-13445 to track fix.

2025-02-15 - Security review: Preliminary sign-off pending resolution of retention policy. Action: set retention to 2 years for elevation events and 7 years for key-signing artifacts per compliance team. Security to re-review on 2025-02-20.
2025-02-15 - Ravi Kapoor: Implemented prototype approval microservice; internal PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/778. Requesting review from security and platform owners.
